proposals.evidence: CDIAL 12598 śṛṇoti explicitly gives Bhojpuri sunal and western suṇṇo “hear”. Eastern -l and western -y inflections can continue the hear stem; sun-lo and ambiguous sunā causative/past forms require local morphology. Reviewed comparison: bagri_fatehabad sūnyɔ “listen!, he heard” (f_nokqsgh4zcjee). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6507.2 *dekṣati gives the dekh- see verb and regional v-/d- variation through transmission. Dekh-ta, dekh-u and ordinary -y past forms retain that stem; dekh-liyo requires the take light verb to be analyzed. Reviewed comparison: Marw dekʰīyo “look!, he saw” (f_gpebrax4uzl3u). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2575 kaḥ punar gives kaun/koṇ/kuṇa “who” and Old Gujarati kuṇaïṃ instrumental. The q/k variants and final pronominal vowels preserve the family; Kalasha kura needs comparison with a different interrogative stem. Reviewed comparison: bagri_fatehabad kūṇ “who?” (f_rjqqkqyelfwxe). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
